suite_note: Shared cross-language CAID conformance vectors for draft-schrock-canonical-action-identifier-04. Each vector carries its own inline type definitions and never references the public registry, except the registry-* vectors, which copy one registry entry each. CAID carries no trust semantics: these vectors test identification only, not authorization, identity, or proof.

format.kinds: decode: decode the input octets as JSON text (Section 2.4); expect {ok} or {ok:false, refusals:["malformed_json"]}. parse: strict CAID parse of input.caid. compute: compute over the input with options suite (input.suite, passed as given, whatever its JSON type; absent means no suite), definitions (the vector member, passed as given) and enum_snapshots (this file); expect {caid, digest, definition_sha256} or {refusals}. verify: verify the input against input.caid with definitions, enum_snapshots and, when present, expected_definition_sha256 (passed as given); expect {valid, reasons, details, definition_sha256?}. definition: definition_sha256 of input.definition; expect {definition_sha256} or {refusals:["invalid_definition"]}.
format.inputs: Exactly one input form: input.json is a string whose UTF-8 encoding is the JSON text; input.json_b64 is the exact octets, base64; input.json_repeat {prefix, unit, count, suffix} is UTF-8(prefix) + count copies of UTF-8(unit) + UTF-8(suffix); input.native is a native-lane value (caid/conformance/runners/native.mjs describes the encoding). A runner calls the byte entry point for the first three forms and, when the octets decode, also the native entry point on the decoded value, and requires identical results. For input.native it builds the host value and calls the native entry point only.
format.relations: relation.same_caid_as / different_caid_from compare the CAIDs the implementation computes for two vectors. time_budget_ms bounds the wall time of the byte entry-point call.

previous_versions.note: Byte digest of the version 1 corpus as last published on main before registry v4. Version 2 adds pinned-enum, inline-enum, own-member, and unpaired-surrogate refusals that the version 1 reference implementations do not enforce.

Byte digest of the version 2 corpus as last published on main (pull request #789). Version 3 adds whole-string grammar refusals (a trailing line feed in an amount, digest field, timestamp, action type, suite, or CAID digest) that the version 2 Python implementation accepted, and value-based integer-field cases (12.0 and 1.2e1 are the integer 12; an out-of-range integer refuses once as unsupported_number) on which the version 2 Python and Go implementations disagreed with the JavaScript reference.

Byte digest of the version 3 corpus as last published on main (pull request #811). Version 4 adds identifier-parse refusals that the version 3 JavaScript, Python, and Go parsers all lacked: a suite that does not begin with a lowercase letter, a suite outside the suite registry, and a digest whose final character sets an unused bit. A registered suite the implementation does not implement still parses.

Byte digest of the version 4 corpus as last published on main (pull request #815), kept byte for byte at caid/conformance/history/vectors.v4.json. Version 5 carries every version 4 vector under the same id with its object as exact JSON text; each of the 22 version 4 vectors that computed a CAID reproduces it (checked by caid/conformance/check-v4.mjs). Results change for six vectors, each by a named -04 rule: three unpaired-surrogate vectors are malformed_json on the byte path (their native-lane twins keep unsupported_value), and the three unregistered-suite vectors are unknown_suite at parse. Every successful compute adds definition_sha256, and every verification adds details and, when a definition resolved, definition_sha256.

vectors.description: hyphens are permitted inside lowercase action-type segments
underscores are outside the registered action-type grammar
registered action-type versions start at one
a common code in the integrity-pinned ISO 4217 snapshot is accepted
a less-common active code in the same pinned ISO 4217 snapshot is accepted
a string absent from the pinned ISO 4217 snapshot fails closed
a mutable external name without snapshot metadata is not a value constraint
pin metadata without an exactly matching locally supplied snapshot fails closed
embedded external values are rejected when their JCS array does not match the declared digest
the compact inline values_ref form is a closed set, not documentation
a values_ref member written as null is present and malformed; it is not the absent-values_ref inline form, even beside a valid values array
a values member written as null beside an inline values_ref is present and must equal the parsed list, so it refuses
inline members are split on | and trimmed of leading and trailing U+0020 SPACE only
a horizontal tab around an inline member is not trimmed, so the member is "\tUSD\t" and USD is outside the set
U+0085 NEXT LINE around an inline member is not trimmed
U+FEFF around an inline member is not trimmed
U+001C FILE SEPARATOR around an inline member is not trimmed
a values array beside an inline values_ref is accepted only when it equals the parsed list exactly
a values array beside an inline values_ref that differs from the parsed list (here only in order) refuses
an external values_ref may embed its pinned array in values; the embedded array is digest-checked like a supplied snapshot
an embedded values member is the snapshot and must verify on its own; an empty one refuses even when a matching snapshot is supplied
a required field named __proto__ that the object does not carry as its own member is missing
an absent optional field named constructor is absent, not an inherited value to type-check
a required field named toString that the object does not carry is missing, not mistyped

cbor-sha256 is in the suite registry, so a CAID naming it parses even in an implementation that does not implement that suite; there, computation and verification report unknown_suite

43 base64url characters carry 258 bits for a 256-bit digest, so the final character's two low bits are unused and must be zero. 'Z' (value 25) sets one and is refused; 'Y' (value 24) is the only encoding of the same 32 octets.
a 44-character digest decodes to 33 octets, not the 32 octets of a jcs-sha256 digest
